title: Model / Vertical branch node
description:
A node in the models/ tree — HOW the domain's motion runs. Sales calls these B2B, PLG and channel; Customer Support calls them tiered, swarming and follow-the-sun. Same mechanism either way.

The tree is real and navigable, but it INHERITS: a capability or object file exists inside a branch only when it genuinely differs from the canonical one. Resolution order is vertical -> model -> canonical. Full copies at every node would produce ~45 divergent decision-maker.yaml files within a month, which is the failure this file's `overrides` and `extends` blocks exist to avoid.

`characteristics` carries two families of key — commercial (buyer, cycle, ACV, committee) and operational (requester, resolution time, volume, staffing, coverage, automation). A branch fills in whichever family describes it and leaves the other absent. They are not alternatives to each other in general: an enterprise support branch legitimately has both a committee and a coverage window.

id.description:
`<domain>.<axis>.<slug>`. The axis segment was `model` for every branch regardless of what it was, which is why the shipped vertical `early_stage_ai_product` carries the id `admin.model.early_stage_ai_product` — readable as a model by anyone grepping for one. Widened rather than rewritten: existing ids stay valid and are not renamed, because an id is what `l3_activation.variant_ids` and every `unresolved_variant_ids` receipt refer to.

THE LAST SEGMENT MUST EQUAL THE FOLDER NAME. `_resolve_variants` matches a declaration against three aliases — the full id, its last dotted segment, and the slugified name — and `variant_ids` holds folder slugs. A branch whose folder says `pm` while its id ends `product_manager` is authored, loaded, and unreachable by the name a tenant declares; `context/tenant_profile.unreachable_slugs` reports that class.

kind.description: Which axis this branch is on. `model` is how the work is run, `vertical` what kind of company it is, `role` who is reading. They share this schema because they are the same SHAPE — a branch that declares only what differs from its parent — and differ only in the question they answer.

parent.description: Parent branch id. null at a top-level model; required on a vertical.

characteristics.description: What is structurally true of running the motion this way. Read by a human deciding whether a tenant fits this branch; never evaluated.

requester.description: Operational branches: who actually contacts support, which is frequently not the buyer. The end user raising a ticket has no commercial relationship with us and no patience for one.

typical_resolution_hours.description: Hours, not days — a consumer chat resolving in 20 minutes and an enterprise defect resolving in three weeks both round badly to days.

volume_shape.description: e.g. high-volume/low-complexity, spiky around releases, seasonal.

staffing_model.description: e.g. tiered L1/L2/L3, swarming, pooled, named engineer.

coverage.description: e.g. 24x7 follow-the-sun, business hours in one region, on-call after hours.

automation_level.description: How much is deflected or resolved before a human sees it.

capabilities.description: Which of the canonical capabilities this branch exercises. Absent means inherit the parent's set unchanged.

activates.description: Capability ids that are in play here and are NOT in the canonical default set.

deactivates.description: Canonical capability ids that do not exist in this motion at all.

emphasises.description: Present in both, but disproportionately important here. Advisory.

extends.description: Branch-local additions to a shared object. This is how the tree stays navigable without duplicating the object.

object.description: Object id being extended. Must resolve.

require_properties.description: Canonical properties that become mandatory in this branch.

overrides.description: Dotted-path overrides against canonical files, e.g. capabilities.sales.qualification.lead_qualification.min_stakeholders: 3. Applied by _tools/index.py in resolution order. Flat map so a diff reads as a diff.

render.description:
How a card must READ for this branch — the same shape and the same slot vocabulary a situation file uses, merged OVER the situation's own copy by `packs/compiler/capability_resolver.variant_render_overlay`. A branch states only the keys it changes; everything it is silent about keeps the canonical wording.

Resolution is role -> vertical -> model -> canonical, most specific last, so a CTO at an AI agency reads a CTO's card. A branch that carries no `render` block leaves the canonical copy object untouched rather than rebuilding it, because this metadata is hashed into the expertise package's content address and an identical-but-rebuilt mapping would re-address knowledge that did not change.

situation_cap.description: Prose character budget for this card, excluding source-verified verbatim quotes. The measured 201-character card was cut to 111; a briefing now declares its budget while existing cards retain 140.

artifact_kind.description: What the attached artifact IS — draft_reply, draft_intro, brief. Also names the card's action button. Defaults to a generic draft when absent.

render_hint.description: The instruction handed to the copy renderer: what the headline, the situation line and the artifact must each say for THIS situation. This is the field that stops every card in a situation type reading alike, so it has to name the specific judgment the reader needs, not restate the situation's description.

fallback.description: The deterministic copy used when no model is available or the render is rejected. It must be honest on its own: it ships to a real user.

states_absence.description:
TRUE when these words describe what is NOT on record rather than what IS. A situation predicated on an absence (matches.when carries an `absent:` clause, or the fallback's whole content is a gap) cannot instruct, because there is nothing to instruct about. Declaring it here makes the card ABSTAIN: it is written at level `review` ("a human must look, and here is the exact question") instead of `prescriptive`, and it does not earn the app or agent surface.

Measured on the design partner's org, 2026-08-30: 47 live cards, every one of them `prescriptive`, and 25 of the 47 said only that something was missing — "errorcore.dev: no problem documented yet", "boardy.ai: no concerns logged yet". 13 came from sales.sit.deal_without_a_stated_problem and 3 from sales.sit.inbound_fit_check, both of which are DEFINED by an absence. The build-time clarity gate that should have caught them (deliver/card_builder.py::clarity_verdict) is keyed on three legacy pack reason codes and matched 0 of the 47.

Do NOT set this on a situation reporting a fact about the WORLD that happens to be negative. "They wrote nine days ago and no reply has gone back" is a finding — somebody is waiting. "Nothing on record says what problem is being solved" is a fact about our own records. That is the line this flag draws.

answerable_for.description:
Corpus domains this ROLE is answerable for. Read by `reason/brief_ranking`: a card whose domain is not in this list steps down 1,500bp in the daily brief, and a card inside it is left exactly where Layer 4 put it — the book pass may only subtract, never raise.

DOMAINS AND NOT CAPABILITIES, deliberately. There are three domains and 534 capabilities; nobody maintains a per-capability remit by hand, and a list nobody maintains is a list that quietly stops being true.

OMITTING IT MEANS 'NOT STATED', AND NOT STATED MEANS NO PENALTY. A reader whose remit nobody wrote down must not have cards pushed down the brief on the strength of an omission. Meaningless on a `model` or `vertical`, which describe a company rather than a reader.
